title: GCD Sort of an Array
summary: Given an integer array nums, you can swap the positions of any two elements if their greatest common divisor (gcd) is greater than 1.
statement: Given an integer array nums, you can swap the positions of any two elements if their greatest common divisor (gcd) is greater than 1. Determine whether it is possible to sort the array in non-decreasing order through such swaps, and return true if it is possible, or false otherwise.
constraints: nums has 1 through 30000 integers from 2 through 100000.
You may swap two positions whenever their current values have gcd greater than one.
Return whether some sequence of allowed swaps can sort nums nondecreasingly.
hints: Values connected through shared prime factors can be permuted within one component.
Union every value with each distinct prime factor, then compare original and sorted values position by position.
Factor values; union(value,factor); require find(nums[i])==find(sorted_nums[i]) whenever values differ.
Allowed swaps generate exactly the factor-connectivity components, and arbitrary permutations are possible inside a connected swap graph.
editorial: Allowed swaps generate exactly the factor-connectivity components, and arbitrary permutations are possible inside a connected swap graph.

tests.explanation: Twenty-one links factors seven and three, allowing the values to reach sorted order.
Five shares no factor with another value and cannot move to its sorted position.
